name: Split-the-Difference Rejection
scenario: Client proposes: "You are at $120,000 and we are at $80,000; let us split the difference and execute at $100,000 right now."
script: "Splitting the difference sounds fair, but $100,000 does not reflect our underlying delivery costs or unit economics. How did you arrive at that figure beyond it being the mathematical midpoint between our positions?"
defense: Hold the midpoint: if it cannot be met, revert to a granular cost audit and delay launch by two months.
originFull: The Compromise Fallacy establishes that splitting the difference appears equitable but often conceals an arbitrary anchor, drawing a negotiator away from an economically rational reservation price.
defenseFull: When an opponent rejects a midpoint compromise: "The midpoint was proposed to eliminate negotiation friction and close this deal immediately. If you cannot meet there, we will revert to a granular cost audit, which will delay project launch by two months."
